name: Canvas 2D fingerprint
plain: Draws text and shapes to a hidden canvas, then hashes the pixels the device produced.
meaning: GPU, driver, OS font rasterizer and anti-aliasing leave tiny pixel differences. The hash is a stable device-class identifier that works with no cookies and no prompt.

steps: fillText with odd fonts plus arcs and gradients
Read pixels with toDataURL or getImageData

data.metric: Hash of 300x150 default canvas pixels (about 180 KB RGBA read out as a string or hash)

fields.name: hash
fields.precision: stable across reloads on the same stack

limits.headline: Can turn a hidden drawing into a device number that works without cookies
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Draw hidden text and shapes, then check the pixels your device made
Create a number from your graphics card, fonts and software
Recognise the same device on later visits, even after cookies are cleared
cannot: Tell exactly who you are by itself
Get exact results from Tor Browser, which asks first, or from Brave, which adds noise
Be turned off by a cookie banner choice

story.what_it_is: A script draws text and shapes in a hidden canvas, then hashes the pixels the device produces.

marketing.name: Firefox fingerprinting protection
marketing.pitch: Firefox says it blocks known fingerprinting scripts and makes canvas readback less unique.

story.for_you: You do not see it. The same drawing looks a little different on different computers because of fonts and graphics chips, so your result works like a quiet ID card.
story.for_makers: Ad tech and fraud vendors use it as one core signal in a bundle. Its value is that it works on most browsers with no permission and stays the same after cookies are cleared.

use_cases.example: A data broker uses the canvas hash to match your phone visit and laptop visit to the same profile.
A payments site flags a checkout when the same canvas hash shows up on hundreds of fake orders.
A game site bans a cheater and then recognizes the same device when they try to make a new account.
A web analytics tool without cookies uses the canvas hash to count unique visits.
A social site blocks a banned user from signing up again from the same device.
A ticket seller finds a single scalper using one browser behind many accounts.
A bank links your new login to your trusted device list without asking for a code every time.

technical_bounds: Pixel output is device class level, not per-device unique: millions of identical hardware and software stacks collide
Cannot identify the person alone; best combined with WebGL, audio and fonts

value.legit_uses: Anti-fraud device ID, bot detection, font and emoji support checks
value.abuse: Cookieless cross-site tracking, fingerprint resale, covert re-identification after cookie clearing

history.change: Mowery and Shacham 'Pixel Perfect' introduces canvas fingerprinting
Acar et al. find AddThis canvas fingerprinting on 5% of top 100k sites
Canvas extraction prompt added under privacy.resistFingerprinting (Tor Uplift)
Canvas noise in Private Browsing (Advanced Fingerprinting Protection)
Randomized canvas readback in Private Browsing and ETP Strict
Fingerprinting protection extended to all browsing for known fingerprinting scripts
